blockers.claim: authorizationRecord is a closed, exact-scope schema for every covered host act and composes with doctor v4's consent record.
blockers.evidence: For CA-1, doctor v4 requires consent bound to the exact component generation identity and admitted manifest digest. authorizationRecord has no componentGenerationIdentity or admittedManifestDigest member. resourceScope is described as resources the act may touch, while FC-C6 merely requires that some admitted manifest exist; neither binds this authorization record to the component bytes actually spawned. A GRANTED-shaped CA-1 record can therefore be replayed across two admitted generations within the same invocation without violating any closed member. The record also uses CA-1-HOST-HEAD/CA-4-HOST and uppercase GRANTED/DENIED while doctor v4's post-report uses CA-1..CA-4 and requested→granted|denied, with no normative field mapping other than effectOutcome.
blockers.requiredRepair: Add required CA-1 target members for exact component generation identity and admitted manifest digest, and make an absent/mismatched value deny. Add a designContractRef to the recorded contract version/digest. Specify a total mapping from every authorizationRecord actionClass, resolution, id/audit identity, and scope field into doctor-v4 consentRecords members, including case/vocabulary conversion, then add cross-generation replay and wrong-manifest fixtures.

blockers.claim: The effect-commit and process-death rules can always emit an honest doctor-v4 effectOutcome without falsely declaring a committed process spawn unperformed.
blockers.evidence: CA-1 defines commit as 'the spawn syscall has returned a live child pid.' A child can be created or begin executing after kernel acceptance but before the parent call returns; cancel or parent death in that window is classified pre-commit and cancellationBeforeCommit mandates DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED, even though a child may exist. Separately, processDeath mandates an INDETERMINATE consent record, while cleanup says doctor writes the record after the fact, there is no pre-commit journal, and no surviving writer/custodian is named. If the process that dies is doctor—the in-scope host actor for CA-3/CA-4—it cannot produce the mandatory post-report. If another process is meant, 'process death' is underdefined. FC-PROCESS-DEATH-INDETERMINATE therefore specifies an oracle the architecture cannot necessarily emit.
blockers.requiredRepair: Move CA-1/CA-2 commit to the irreversible OS process-creation acceptance boundary, not parent observation, and define the race when acceptance is unknown. Name which process death ends authorization. Provide a surviving supervisor or durable pre-attempt/commit-intent carrier with custody and recovery rules that can write INDETERMINATE after doctor death, or explicitly bound the guarantee and route the missing crash report to an owner instead of claiming the fixture passes. Test cancel/death during the syscall, child-created-before-return, and crash after effect commit but before report persistence.

blockers.claim: slice1EgressExecutionSide gives every spawned-process egress a lawful, non-circular actor/authorization owner.
blockers.evidence: ES-2 says every send by a process doctor spawned—including a CA-2 customer tool—is 'component-originated egress, exclusively DR-105 / PT-NET-EGRESS.' Permission v1's PT-NET-EGRESS REQUESTED state requires an admitted component manifest permissions[] declaration. Doctor v4 defines CA-2 as a customer-owned external tool outside OpenSIP's signed closure, and this artifact's own actorSet puts only admitted component children outside scope as DR-105 actors. PATH-SPAWNED-TOOL-EGRESS then calls the actor COMPONENT-OR-UNBOUNDED-TOOL, says 'Not this contract,' and concedes host CA-4 does not authorize its sockets, but names no other authority and only conditionally refuses it when a separate host CA-4 is absent. A customer tool is not made a component by being spawned, cannot obtain PT-NET-EGRESS, and is not a doctor-process host CA-4. The D-032 egress assignment therefore terminates for components but not for CA-2 tools.
blockers.requiredRepair: Split ES-2 into admitted-component and customer-tool branches. Keep admitted component egress exclusively in DR-105. For CA-2 tool egress, either make every network-capable tool execution unexercisable under the current slice, or route a distinct product/authorization decision to a named owner under D-000; do not assign PT-NET-EGRESS without an admitted manifest. Reconcile doctor v4's separate-CA-4 recital with the selected actor rule and add a fixture proving host CA-4 can never authorize a tool's own socket.

advisories.claim: CA-3 admission ownership and standing use one non-contradictory state model.
advisories.evidence: OUT_OF_ROOT_READ and LOCAL_SOCKET_OR_PIPE name Operability+security jointly with Security+platform as productAdmissionAuthority, then label their standing UNOWNED-FOR-ADMISSION and prescribe D-000 owner assignment only if those named owners decline. An absent admission is OPEN/NOT-ADMITTED, not unowned when an accountable authority is already named.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Use OPEN-NOT-ADMITTED for subtypes with named owners and reserve UNOWNED for PRIVILEGED_PLATFORM_FACILITY until D-000 assigns one. Keep every state fail-closed.

advisories.claim: A per-invocation authorization record is auditable against the exact recorded design contract and exact product-admission evidence.
advisories.evidence: FC-C1 relies on global knowledge that the design contract was recorded, while authorizationRecord has no design-contract path/digest/version member. productAdmissionRefs are required but have no closed shape, digest, selector, authority, or standing fields. Two records with identical visible members may therefore have been evaluated under different contract versions or unverifiable admission prose.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Add a structured designContractRef and close productAdmissionRefs over authority, decision/artifact path, selector, digest, standing, and scope. Make stale or moved references deny and add replay-after-supersession fixtures.
